doc.title: Elvin Jones — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Ellington, Gil Evans and first own groups
title: Forming a trio with Jimmy Garrison and Joe Farrell
summary: After the Ellington tour he formed a piano-less trio, which recorded 'Putting It Together'.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: Okay, well let’s try to get back where we were. You had just left the Duke Ellington Orchestra now.
Well, I think I heard Keiko mention earlier that was in March of 1966. What happened after that?

Well, when that tour was over I came back to New York. We talked about…I said, “I should get a group of my own, I’m tired of playing with everybody else.” Anyway, I found that. I called up Jimmy Garrison, I called up Joe Farrell, and I knew him very well so we got a trio together and I got a trio.
And we did that first piece, “Putting It Together”.
